\section[la tasa]{la tasa — the tax, the fee; the rate}

\label{lesson:ES-C663-tasa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the penalty, then the Spanish for the cancellation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la tasa}
\textbf{la tasa} — \textquotedblleft{}the tax, the fee; the rate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El hotel cobra una tasa turística.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The hotel charges a tourist tax.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La tasa turística} — the tourist tax. \emph{La tasa de paro} — the unemployment rate.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tasa} is built on \emph{tasar} \textquotedblleft{}to value, to set a price on\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{taxāre} \textquotedblleft{}to assess, to rate\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la tasa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la tasa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la tasa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the penalty, then the Spanish for the cancellation, then say \emph{la tasa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la tasa mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The tax, the fee; the rate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el suplemento]{el suplemento — the extra charge, the supplement}

\label{lesson:ES-C663-suplemento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the cancellation, then the Spanish for the tax.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el suplemento}
\textbf{el suplemento} — \textquotedblleft{}the extra charge, the supplement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La cama extra tiene un suplemento.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There is an extra charge for the extra bed.}
\end{quote}

A newspaper \emph{suplemento} is a magazine inside it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{suplemento} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{supplēmentum} \textquotedblleft{}that which makes a thing full, a supply\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short; EtymDB), from \emph{supplēre} \textquotedblleft{}to fill up\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el suplemento}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el suplemento}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el suplemento}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the cancellation, then the Spanish for the tax, then say \emph{el suplemento} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el suplemento mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The extra charge, the supplement\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la fianza]{la fianza — the deposit, the security; bail}

\label{lesson:ES-C663-fianza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the tax, then the Spanish for the extra charge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la fianza}
\textbf{la fianza} — \textquotedblleft{}the deposit, the security; bail\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hay que dejar una fianza de cien euros.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{You have to leave a hundred-euro deposit.}
\end{quote}

For a rented flat, the deposit is \emph{la fianza}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{fianza} is built on \emph{fiar} \textquotedblleft{}to vouch for\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), which comes from Vulgar Latin \emph{fīdāre}, Latin \emph{fīdere} \textquotedblleft{}to trust\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la fianza}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la fianza}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la fianza}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the tax, then the Spanish for the extra charge, then say \emph{la fianza} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[el reembolso]{el reembolso — the refund}

\label{lesson:ES-C663-reembolso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the extra charge, then the Spanish for the deposit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el reembolso}
\textbf{el reembolso} — \textquotedblleft{}the refund\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pedí el reembolso del billete.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I asked for a refund on the ticket.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Contra reembolso} — cash on delivery.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reembolso} is built on \emph{reembolsar}, from \emph{re-} and \emph{embolsar} \textquotedblleft{}to put in the purse\textquotedblright{}; \emph{bolsa} comes from Late Latin \emph{bursa}, from Greek \emph{býrsa} \textquotedblleft{}hide\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el reembolso}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el reembolso}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the extra charge, then the Spanish for the deposit, then say \emph{el reembolso} again
\end{itemize}

\section[reembolsar]{reembolsar — to refund, to pay back}

\label{lesson:ES-C663-reembolsar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the deposit, then the Spanish for the refund.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: reembolsar}
\textbf{reembolsar} — \textquotedblleft{}to refund, to pay back\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Le reembolsamos el dinero en tres días.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We will refund your money within three days.}
\end{quote}

Close to \emph{devolver el dinero}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reembolsar} is built from \emph{re-} \textquotedblleft{}back\textquotedblright{} and \emph{embolsar} \textquotedblleft{}to put in the purse\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{bolsa}, from Late Latin \emph{bursa}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
